title: mini-canary-solo-notebook
content:
Notes to self: running a very small, solo mini-canary for KV-cache tuning (ttl + prefix evict) — aim is to validate warmup behavior and no-tail-latency regressions for hosted API path. Keep it tiny, reversible, and observable.

Primary hypothesis:
- Small change to KV eviction TTL reduces cold-token generation by ~8% after warmup for typical 1024-token flows.
- No customer-facing 5xx or latency p99 regressions.

Quick goals (success criteria):
- No 5xx spike > 0.1% relative in first 60m.
- P99 latency change <= +10ms vs baseline for the pinned cohort.
- Cache hit ratio increases by at least 3 percentage points for warm requests within cohort.

Scope & constraints:
- Only touch hosted-api runtime config: kv.default_ttl and kv.prefix_eviction (alpha flag).
- Target a single region (us-west1) and a single tiny cohort (client_id prefix = test-mini-2026).
- Traffic fraction: start 0.05% -> 0.5% -> 2% (if green) over ~4 hours.
- Rollback must be a single API call (see kill-switch below).

Preflight checklist (do not skip):
- [ ] Confirm PR merged + image deployed to staging cluster: runtime:sha-2483
- [ ] Load test local warmup script against staging (warmup 1000 short requests) — observe cache hit curve
- [ ] Create canary cohort in routing: route rule ID: rc-mini-2026-1 (work w/ routing eng if needed)
- [ ] Update monitoring dashboard with baseline windows (last 72h) and pin comparison range
- [ ] Alert hooks: pager for 5xx_rate, slack burn channel for p99_autotrack; set temporary severity mapping
- [ ] Notify on-call SRE + product owner in #deploy-alerts Slack 30m before start

Start plan:
1) 00:00 - smoke sanity (0.05% traffic) – 15m
   - Run quick canary script: ./tools/canary-shift --cohort=mini-2026 --fraction=0.0005 --duration=15m
   - Validate: 5xx_rate, p99, cache_hit_ratio on dashboard
   - Manual check: sample 10 traces (span search) for unexpected errors

2) 00:20 - expand to 0.5% – 45m
   - ./tools/canary-shift --cohort=mini-2026 --fraction=0.005 --duration=45m
   - Watch for any stepstair increases in tail latency or new error codes from runtime (KV EVICT errors)

3) 01:10 - expand to 2% – 2h
   - Only if previous windows green; consider A/B compare with baseline cohort using traffic mirroring for deeper trace sampling

Kill-switches / rollback:
- Immediate rollback (fast): routing API call to remove cohort rule (route_rule.remove rc-mini-2026-1).
- Runtime revert (if image-level): roll image back to runtime:sha-2480 via deploy tool: ./ops/deploy --image=runtime:sha-2480 --region=us-west1 --service=hosted-api
- Emergency throttle: block traffic to cohort with iptables rule on edge proxies (SRE assistance)

Operational commands (cheat sheet):
- check current cohort fraction: ./tools/canary-status --cohort=mini-2026
- roll forward/back: ./tools/canary-shift --cohort=mini-2026 --fraction=<frac>
- remove rule: ./tools/canary-remove --cohort=mini-2026
- force rollback image: ./ops/deploy --image=runtime:sha-2480 --service=hosted-api --region=us-west1

Telemetry to watch (short list):
- 5xx_rate_by_route (hosted-api) — absolute and relative to baseline
- p50/p95/p99 latency for completion and first-byte
- cache_hit_ratio and kv_eviction_rate
- token_generation_time (median, p99)
- tail-end sign: increased retries from SDKs, spike in client backoffs
- error taxon: any new error codes logged by runtime (tag: kv.*)

Post-deploy validations (0–4h):
- Golden-test suite (10k sanity requests) against cohort: pass rate >= 99.5%
- Compare epoch averages: cache_hit_ratio delta, token_time delta
- Collect 200 sampled traces for deep inspection (trace id list saved to /tmp/mini-canary-traces.txt)
- Metric: rolling 1h window p99 within +10ms, 5xx <= +0.1%

Notes to self / lessons to capture:
- Keep cohort ID short and searchable (mini-2026).
- Prefer single-region first; cross-region can introduce noisy baselines.
- If cache_hit_ratio improves but no latency drop — probable telemetry sampling miss (verify span-level timings).
- Remember: SDK clients that pin tokens aggressively will mask cache improvements; instruct SDK owners on warmup expectations.

Open questions / TODOs:
- [ ] Confirm whether function-calling jobs are affected by eviction TTL (ENG-6529 follow-up).
- [ ] Add a lightweight synthetic that specifically exercises long context retrieval (2000-token warmups).
- [ ] Should we capture kv.trace_id on eviction events? (would help correlate re-gen spikes)

Post-mortem headings (pre-populate):
- Summary of change
- Timeline (timestamps + operator)
- Metrics before/after (graphs + numbers)
- Root cause (if rollback needed)
- Action items (owners + eta)

Housekeeping commands (handy):
- tail logs for cohort: kla logs --service=hosted-api --filter='cohort:mini-2026' --follow
- sample traces: tracing-tool query --filter='cohort=mini-2026' --limit=200 > /tmp/mini-canary-traces.txt
- snapshot dashboard: dashboard-tool snapshot --id=dk-mini-2026 --out=mini-2026-dash.png

If anything weird happens: pause expansion, escalate to SRE on-call, and capture a 15m debug dump (metrics + logs + 50 traces) before any rollback — we may need the data for root cause.

Final thought: tiny and focused wins are easier to reason about. Keep the blast radius minimal and metrics front-and-center.

-- Morgan
(last updated: 2026-02-20)
